title: Open up the SPL16 bulk interior
description:
The widest remaining bet. Match reconstruction was the largest single difference in the checked-block gap, and C amortizes checks across a wider interior: it stops checking history underflow once the produced prefix covers all representable offsets, and its bulk copies use a padded contract. Rust's two-token batch falls back in more classes.

Start with a census of why the batch exits (extended literal or match, actual overlap, insufficient initialized room, dictionary or history, tail) and attach the samples to those classes. Use `single`, match-heavy `mozilla` and `webster`, and `sao` with zero extended matches. If ordinary tokens dominate, try hoisting checks over a proven interior with initialized output room and enough prior history to cover all representable offsets, keeping the checked terminal and dictionary path. If overlap owns the residual, pick one common measured distance class. C's wider bulk loop is a reference, not permission to rely on its scratch padding. No bundle of entropy and LZ changes.

title: Avoid rebuilding contiguous dictionary history for each small block

acceptance_criteria: Measure copied bytes and throughput for small blocks with large dictionaries and for dictionary-free controls. Cover matches crossing from dictionary to output, overlapping matches, concatenated frames and ID zero. Check exact archive bytes and reference decode.

title: Profile and speed up Dense match selection
description:
The bit-priced parser made Dense smaller than before, at 5.6x and 2.3x the old encode wall time on the two study inputs. The next encode-speed pass starts with match selection: on the final binary, `perf record -e cycles:u -F 997` put 89% of `dickens` and 78% of `sao` self samples in Parser::parse, including inlined helpers.

Hold archive sizes alongside every timing; reducing the probe limit can give back some of the ratio win. Try scalar constant-cost relaxation over the current spans before SoA layouts, SIMD, epoch heads or deeper searches. Measure chain hops, tag rejects, extension bytes, DP relax attempts and updates, reset and write traffic, and footprint. Treat any change to span, price or depth as a separate size-encode-decode experiment, and do not pay for 512 KiB full-block state or depth 128 just to mimic C7.

title: Charge a decode tax for Dense literal Huffman sections
description:
C adds a per-level decode tax when it selects candidates. Test the same idea for new Dense archives: require inline Huffman literals to beat raw by a margin, computed as an exact integer ceiling in bytes on the descriptor-adjusted payload. One scratch build swept 0%, 1%, 2% and 4% over the frozen Silesia corpus with both decoders held fixed. The token path never entered the new branch.

Rejected; Dense keeps its 0% policy. Every positive threshold stayed under the 1% corpus size budget, but none delivered a credible 5% full-corpus serial wall-time reduction on either decoder. At 4%, Rust used 5.70% less serial CPU but took only 3.36% less wall time, with variation that allows no wall gain. Without `sao` the CPU gain disappeared, and pinned C showed no corresponding gain. The tradeoff is real where Huffman barely wins: `sao` alone fell 44% in wall time for Rust and 21% for C at 4%. Encode CPU rose in every pass at 4%.

title: Pack Dense Huffman runs with compact per-symbol routes
description:
`perf record -e cycles:u` attributed 40.9% of 723 Dense encode samples on `dickens` to Tree::emit. The writer kept a separately allocated list of (run, code, width) tuples for each symbol and updated two destination bytes on every step, including single bits that could never cross a byte boundary. Keep a compact route per symbol instead: the prefix identifies single-bit runs, and only the terminal run can need a multi-bit write. An inline table and its payload share one allocation. Candidate pricing still uses each run's byte-rounded length.

Result: with the parser held fixed, all 12 Silesia archives were byte-identical. Median whole-CLI encode time fell from 121.5 to 109.5 ms on `dickens` and 133.7 to 116.3 ms on `sao`. In a scalar Wasmtime component the Criterion encode interval went from 142.75-148.86 to 130.02-131.19 ms on `dickens` (10 samples, sequential runs).

title: Use a bounded bit-priced match parser for Dense
description:
Replace Dense's greedy matches with a parser that chooses matches by estimated bit cost: at most 24 predecessors per lookup in a 64 KiB window, shorter endpoints considered at the same offset, and one best predecessor per endpoint over 32 KiB spans. The final serializer still prices the exact entropy sections and can select RAW. Heads, predecessor ring and parse states use about 896 KiB per Dense worker; pure Split and Packed workloads never allocate them.

Result: on the two study inputs, Dense archives shrank 20.3% on `dickens` and 9.9% on `sao`, both then smaller than pinned C7. Over all of Silesia the sum of the 12 archives fell from 82,530,245 to 70,459,885 bytes (-14.6%), narrowing the gap to C7 from 17.7% to 0.49%. The tradeoff is encode time: 5.6x and 2.3x the old Dense wall time on the two inputs.

title: Report compression and fixed-archive decode against pinned C in one command
description:
`cargo xtask comparison-report` answers two questions from one run: how fast the current CLI compresses and at what size, and how fast it reads the same existing archives as upstream. It builds and saves the Rust CLI, fetches and builds C `5719a96f`, stages hash-checked C archives at levels 1-7, cross-decodes every staged archive with every decoder before timing, and publishes `report.md`, `summary.tsv` and `raw.json` only after verification, sampling and rendering succeed.

The second schema adds what old wall times cannot recover: decode worker counts, child CPU cost per plaintext GB, an optional concatenated-frame control, and a saved earlier Rust CLI as a `--before` baseline. It prints the matrix size and CPU budget first and warns `CONSTRAINED` when affinity or a cgroup quota is below the largest requested worker count.

The first sweep found decode closest on separate files and far behind on concatenated frames, before worker reuse; its worker rankings were tentative on a busy host.

title: Replay checked C7 blocks and Huffman sections against pinned C on one core
description:
Remove the frame drivers and time the worker kernels on the exact bytes: the 405 checked blocks of the long C7 frame and its original inline Huffman sections, with `mozilla` and `sao` as controls. Rust calls BlockDecoder::decode with the parsed header and an exact body slice into initialized Vec scratch. C calls the runtime dispatcher its file worker uses, with its padded fast-output contract. Both verify every block checksum and fold the same fingerprint on each timed pass. Grouped userspace cycles and instructions attach to one resident thread and must run at 100%.

Findings, in order. C used 38.9% / 39.8% less thread CPU than portable Release Rust on the long frame, about 0.22-0.23 CPU seconds per plaintext GB. Separate stage clocks put the difference in section preparation (+0.16 elapsed s/GB) and reconstruction (+0.10), with no checksum difference. In isolated sections C AVX2 used 1.92 cycles per symbol for literals and tokens against portable Rust's 4.87 / 5.28, and the gap survived target-cpu=native. Leaf-IP attribution then split Rust's excess checked-block cycles into about 38% reconstruction, 26% gather, 19% unpack, 10% table setup and 5% copy-back. Those shares predate width six and the AVX2 merge.

title: Batch pairs of inline sequences in two-byte SPL reconstruction
description:
Take two inline tokens together when both use two-byte offsets and their matches fit entirely in already-produced plaintext. One bound covers the fixed-width stores; either token can cause the pair to fall back to the checked loop, and the first token is kept when the second needs the fallback.

Result: in 15 shuffled passes on the same Dense archives, median elapsed time per corpus pass fell from 218.8 to 188.1 ms (14%), with `webster` benefiting most (45.61 to 34.94 ms). An independent seven-pass check on the frozen probe gave per full pass: Dense 224.3 to 196.3, C3 138.6 to 104.1, C7 206.0 to 178.4 ms. Kept despite a small-block tradeoff: in a 31-pass control repeat, synthetic `same-prefix` was 6% slower and 4 KiB-block `sao` 8% slower.

title: Use bounded short copies for SPL and PAK reconstruction
description:
Select the token layout outside the loop and use bounded 8- or 16-byte copies for common short runs. Only the logical prefix is valid output and history; a real overlap or a dictionary-boundary match still uses the checked path.

Result: with entropy held fixed, `zxc test` time fell from 30.6 to 18.2 ms on Dense `dickens`, and from 20.4 to 8.6 ms on raw-section C3 `dickens`. Those are isolated `test` results; they do not include writing plaintext to stdout.

title: Unpack fixed-width PivCo groups and enable runtime SIMD in the CLI
description:
`perf record -e cycles:u` attributed 75% of old `sao` cycles to Tree::decode. Decode a pair of leaves directly from its bitmap, unpack groups of eight fixed-width symbols from exactly their on-wire bytes, and count complete words when sizing mixed runs. The native CLI enables the runtime-selected SIMD merge by default; scalar builds remain available.

Result: with reconstruction held fixed, `sao` went from 30.6 ms to 23.2 ms with the scalar changes and to 16.2 ms with the SIMD merge. In a separate scalar WIT measurement the Huffman change took `sao` from 50.3 to 44.1 ms (Criterion point estimates). This is the scalar group loop that the width-three and width-six kernels later specialize.

title: Reuse Huffman byte buffers per decode worker
description:
BlockDecoder owns independent literal and token Vecs and one merge Vec shared by the two Huffman sections in sequence, instead of allocating them for every section. New capacity is reserved exactly on growth; later smaller sections keep initialized tails but do not read or publish them. RAW still borrows the input and RLE still owns its temporary result. Traversal order, queue and inline codebook allocations are unchanged.

For a validated block with frame limit B the three capacities sum to at most 2B + floor(B/5). The first block of a smaller frame discards capacity above the new bound.

Result: serial Rust took 10.8-12.8% less wall time on fixed Dense `sao` and 6.4-8.1% less on fixed C7 `sao`, with matching child CPU savings. Dense `sao` needed seven byte-buffer allocations or growths instead of 56. Full-corpus gains were modest, four-worker wall did not reliably improve, and the default scalar WIT component showed no repeatable `sao` win.

title: Lend the PivCo traversal queue across sections
description:
After the byte-buffer reuse, the traversal FIFO still started cold for every Huffman section: 768 allocation or growth events against 1,024 traversal events on 4 KiB mixed input. Lend each worker an empty VecDeque for literal and token sections in sequence and keep it after a successful section only if it holds at most 16 entries. The cap limits retention, not admission. No bitmap address, merge record, gather or copy-back changes.

Rejected. Serial 4 KiB mixed lost 765 of 768 FIFO events (99.61%), but wall time fell only 4.0% / 0.9% across the two series, short of 5% in both. Correctness and memory bounds passed. Fewer allocations alone are not acceptance evidence.

title: Two-group AVX2 PivCo mixed merge
description:
A bounded lane-local shuffle trial on the retained copy-back layout: the two 128-bit lanes of one AVX2 vpshufb gather one eight-output group each, with the original mask table. Fewer shuffle instructions did not mean fewer retired instructions; range and chunk checks, stack spills and lane assembly survived in the timed binary.

Rejected. Long-frame literals used 12.5% more cycles, tokens 10.0% more and checked blocks 6.5% more, with resolved regressions on `sao`. W1 throughput fell 2.95% / 4.73%. Do not retry pairing groups or alternating scratch layouts. The mechanism that did land emits a full 32 bytes per step (zxcrs-perf-decode-merge).

title: Unpack three-bit flat Huffman groups with a bounded x86 byte shuffle
description:
Inline DWARF put width three at 11.15% of long-literal samples in portable Rust. Process 16 decoded symbols from exactly six readable bytes using the eight-entry code-to-symbol table, selected only for eight-entry tables with at least one full 16-symbol group. The caller bounds the entire run and the final 0-15 symbols use the existing scalar routine, so there is no read past the run, padding contract or unsafe. SSE2-only and other targets keep the scalar unpack.

Result: 8.1% fewer cycles per Huffman literal, 5.2% fewer per token and 4.4% fewer per checked plaintext byte on the long C7 frame, with 23 of 24 pairs favoring the candidate. The `sao` checked-block control did not resolve a change, and eight-worker CLI timings were too variable to establish a gain.

title: Put regular-file body reads on the decode workers
description:
Trial: the caller reads only the next eight-byte block header and hands its file position and the existing credit buffer to a worker, which preads the body, revalidates the header and extent, and calls the unchanged decoder. Sixteen credits, ordered commit and the footer barrier stay. Selection happens once on the open handle, so pipes, stdin and non-regular files keep the stream path.

Kept out of production. Coordinator CPU inside successful block admissions fell about 96%, but the work moved rather than disappeared: clean W8/K16 wall on the long `single` frame was 5.1% / 2.0% slower against the parent, and `concat` moved +1.0% / -4.4%. Both single intervals exclude the required 10% gain. The 3% CPU ceiling and pipe nonregression were unresolved. Do not adopt the selector or infer anything about the serial codec from this result.

title: Measure interior worker idle and reader CPU on the landed decoder
description:
The next input-side step if W8 wall still matters, and the precondition for any reader change. Neither another positioned-read rewrite nor a bigger queue is justified by the old coordinator CPU savings alone, and the earlier wait traces predate worker reuse, width six and the AVX2 merge.

On the landed decoder and the intended sink, measure per frame the interior empty-queue wait while blocks remain, worker idle, and the coordinator's `next` split into on-CPU resize, header and copy-on-read time against off-CPU scheduling time. Compare `/dev/null` with a real sink, and a warm file with a preloaded slice. The four-worker probe's interior definition can be ported per frame to the persistent pool; the positioned trial's optional interior reducer was never implemented.

title: Measure where four Crossbeam decode workers wait
description:
Test whether a missing ordered head leaves workers without jobs while input remains to admit. A diagnostic-only build instruments the existing blocking calls in the Crossbeam loop with one process-wide monotonic clock and preallocated thread-private records, then reduces the trace by interval intersection.

Finding: keep eight slots as the four-worker baseline and do not redesign ordered delivery on this evidence. The conservative idle intersection from a missing ordered head is 0.29-0.46 ms per `mozilla` frame; empty-queue idle while the coordinator is in `next` is 2.02-2.19 ms on `mozilla` and 0.75-0.84 ms on `sao`. A later source and sink sensitivity run supports prioritizing the input-side service gap on `mozilla`. These are elapsed intervals in a diagnostic build, not measured speedups.

title: Reuse Crossbeam decode workers and scratch across frames
description:
A syscall trace on the archived eight-worker CLIs counted 96 Rust thread creations against 9 for C on one bundle. Put the lifetime of compute resources under the decode operation: Crossbeam keeps its threads, bounded window and scratch across frames with equal block limits, and drops them on a change of block limit even if the next frame is empty. The caller still drains verified output in order and validates the footer before reading the next frame.

Result: at eight workers on the 12 checksummed C7 frames, wall fell 41-42% and child CPU 23% against the parent, and worker starts went from 96 to 8. All seven parallel counts improved in both series. With stdout to a regular file it saved 18.1% / 18.7% wall at eight workers. There was no single-frame gain (+1.1% / -0.3%). A faster multi-frame pipeline, not a faster block decoder.

title: Retest compact inline Huffman decode tables
description:
The most developed smaller candidate: implemented and verified, not landed. From the canonical lengths it builds per-depth first prefixes and leaf and internal bases, then walks runs in depth order from one fixed 4,080-byte stack array. That replaces the heap nodes, lookup allocations, traversal FIFO and reverse-order Vec while keeping the landed unpack and gather kernels, the encoder and the cached dictionary path.

It missed its original combined 5% gate in the second series, and dropping it on that number was the wrong call. Literals saved 7-8%, tokens 20-21% and checked instructions 3.35%; W1 gained 3.4-5.2%; one entropy-heavy native scalar 4 KiB fixture gained 68-71%. Reopen as a small-block and serial candidate, not as a rewrite budget.

title: Race BMI2 byte deposit against the AVX2 bitmap merge
description:
A 2 KiB table turns eight branch bits into a 64-bit mask; two PDEPs and one OR place the next left and right bytes directly in output order, unrolled four words per 32 outputs. No SIMD lane construction, shuffle-control assembly or partial-lane store.

Dropped on the measured Zen 3. Deposit beat the old kernel by 24.9% / 22.8% fewer gather cycles, but the 32-output AVX2 loop beat deposit head to head by 23.5% / 20.8%. It would also need a measured CPU allowlist, because PDEP is slow on Zen 2; BMI2 support alone is not a speed guarantee. The AVX2 arm landed as zxcrs-perf-decode-merge.

title: SPL16: shrink the copy for 20-32 byte match extensions
description:
Trial 1 of the original ranking. For an already eligible 20-32 byte match extension, snapshot and store 32 initialized bytes instead of the 64-byte copy_within, keeping the 33-64 byte path, the initialized-room guard and all fallbacks.

Rejected. About 4.7% of `single` tokens qualified, but the old 64-byte copy already inlined as four loads and four stores. The split added a length branch and 0.27% more instructions; checked cycles moved +0.72% / +1.11% on `single` and missed the 5% gate. No CLI run was justified. Do not try a ladder of copy widths.

title: Vectorize six-bit PivCo flat unpack on AVX2
description:
Width-six flat runs carry 24% of the long frame's literal symbols and 35% of its flat-unpack samples, yet were decoded by a scalar table lookup per symbol. Add an AVX2 kernel that takes an exact 24-byte group and emits 32 symbols: two 16-byte loads, one window shuffle, four table shuffles with three blends, and one 32-byte store. Dispatch once per subtree on the existing merge-simd feature for runs of at least 32 symbols. Shorter runs, the final 0-31 symbols, other tiers and no-feature builds keep the scalar path.

Result: saved width-six runs used 83% fewer cycles and whole `single` literals 6.7-7.0% fewer. Checked blocks retired 2.27% fewer instructions per byte, with every cycle interval crossing zero. Landed `single` W1 moved +1.63% / +1.45%, the second interval crossing zero. Landed as a verified kernel win, not a confirmed whole-CLI speedup.

Landed single W1 moved +1.63% / +1.45% with the second interval crossing zero, so the end-to-end gain is unresolved. 70 locked release workspace tests and 36 no-default-features codec tests passed; scalar .text is byte-identical. title: Merge PivCo bitmaps in bounded AVX2 tiles
description:
Mixed bitmap gather was about 26% of Rust's checked-block excess over C once width six landed. The old kernel produced eight outputs per step and checked both child windows each time. On x86-64 AVX2, for nodes of at least 128 outputs, emit 32 per step: two 16-output lanes, two vpshufb, one blend and one full 32-byte store, selected by a 20 KiB compile-time table. Both 32-byte child windows must lie inside the counted node, so no padding, wire slack or unsafe code is involved. The loop hands exact cursors to the existing eight-output path, which matters: a direct scalar suffix regressed 86.2% on sparse right-minority runs and 20.1% when that child drained early.

Result: gather cycles fell 43% on the original runs and checked `single` blocks 8.5% / 9.7%. Against its parent the landed kernel gained 7.9-10.2% at W1 and 8.0-8.6% at W8 on `single`. Against pinned C on one core, `single` W1 shows no resolved difference; W8 favors C by 7.5% / 2.9%, the second unresolved, at 18-20% more CPU per GB. On the original 12-frame concat there is no repeatable winner against C and Rust uses 10-15% more CPU per GB.

title: Build canonical Huffman trees with depth buckets
description:
Tree::new sorted the 256 (depth, symbol) pairs for every inline Huffman table, and an older token profile put 16.9% of its samples in that setup. Count the symbols per depth instead, check the same Kraft sum and depth-one singleton case, then place symbols in ascending order at each depth's bucket cursor. The encoder shares this path, so the change is not decode-only.

Result: a quieter targeted repeat measured 8.3% fewer `single` token cycles and 2.7% fewer checked-block cycles per plaintext byte. Two 24-pair CLI series resolved no wall contrast at W1 or W8 on `single`, `mozilla` or `sao`. Kept as a codec-level win, not a W8 claim.

description: Build three same-interface Wasm artifacts, validate ISA requirements, exercise all under Wasmtime and compare repeated wide, mixed and RAW timings.

title: Attribute host/guest list transfers and guest buffer staging
description: Trace a WIT call in both directions, distinguishing canonical ABI transfers from extra copies made by bindings, host helpers or guest codec entry points. Use paired native and Wasmtime benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Report attributable bytes and transfer cost by payload size with a no-codec or equivalent control. Prototype a compatible ownership improvement if one is measurable; document any API change separately.
notes: 2026-11-24 evidence (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37). The wide decode ABI argument is 12,819 B (0.7824 B/B) and the result 16,384 B (1.0): lengths of lists crossing the API, not measured physical transfers (doc/profiling/ledger.md#interpreting-the-rankings). Reused-workspace native, one-shot native and component measured 132.1 / 132.5 / 113.5 MiB/s on the 16 KiB upstream decode (doc/profiling/README.md#compare-native-and-component). Whole-call WIT results depend on the ISA variant (doc/profiling/pivco-merge.md#strict-vs-relaxed-wasm-components), and the typed host instantiates outside timing (doc/profiling/pivco-queue.md#timing-protocol-and-reproduction). Measure the size sweep under zxcrs-perf-boundary first.

title: Verify buffer reuse across worker, reorder and writer handoffs
description: Track backing buffers across encode.rs/block.rs swaps, worker completion, pending slots and in-order writes. Audit reallocations after warm-up and compare the Rayon batch path. Do not count channel movement of Vec handles as byte copying.
acceptance_criteria: Report bytes copied and capacities retained per slot and worker for RAW/mixed blocks, including a slow head. Hold worker/slot budgets fixed; preserve ordered cancellation, serial identity and memory bounds.
notes: 2026-11-24 evidence (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37). Worker, window and scratch reuse across frames landed in 7d6492a0 (doc/profiling/decode-pool.md, zxcrs-parallel-pool); it produced no single-frame gain, and first-write and frame-completion p95 were not measured. The ledger already separates capacity growth from requests that fit an existing capacity and records that moves, swaps and channel handoffs transfer ownership without payload bytes (doc/profiling/ledger.md). The budget to verify is K circulating block buffers plus at most W reconstruction buffers plus private worker entropy scratch (design/decode-throughput/design0.astra.md#the-first-implementation-experiment), against the gates in design/decode-throughput/design0.astra.md#decision-and-promotion-gates. Per-worker Huffman buffer retention is bounded at 2B + floor(B/5) for frame limit B (doc/profiling/pivco-worker.md#what-changed).

title: Reduce staging on repeated in-memory and file range reads
description: Slice ReadAt copies into a block body and each copy_range call owns scratch. Evaluate borrowed archive slices or a reusable range-reader session; compare with positioned file reads.
acceptance_criteria: Report copied/read bytes per requested byte for tiny, aligned and cross-block ranges. Distinguish full-block checksum/decode requirements from avoidable staging. Keep counting-source, forged-entry and concurrent read tests passing.
notes: 2026-11-24 evidence (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37). A 4 KiB result stages 2.002 B/B at 4 KiB blocks and 128.001 at 512 KiB, which also zeroes 128.001; slice and file stage the same lengths. The 512 KiB short range took 33.90-33.94 µs from a slice and 45.41-46.70 µs from a warm file (doc/profiling/ledger.md#interpreting-the-rankings). Borrowing from a slice can remove staging, but the full touched block must still be verified. crates/seek/src/lib.rs already has a cursor-independent positioned-read primitive (design/decode-throughput/design0.astra.md#if-the-session-is-not-the-answer), and scratch belongs to a read, not the shared index (doc/architecture/indexed-execution.md#indexed-reads-first).

title: Audit block input, RAW passthrough and output buffering
description: Compare memory slices, file and pipe paths through frame.rs and the CLI. Identify redundant staging or zero-fill before read_exact, BufReader/BufWriter bypass and any benefit of borrowed or caller-owned buffers.
acceptance_criteria: Separate kernel/user transfers, required writes and redundant user-space passes. Benchmark both small/large blocks and partial I/O; preserve byte limits, short reads and checksum-before-write.
notes: 2026-11-24 evidence (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37), by site. RAW passthrough is already one body read and one output write per plaintext byte (doc/profiling/ledger.md#interpreting-the-rankings), and Rust hands RAW back as a verified slice into the input (doc/profiling/pipeline-comparison.sol.md#decode-sections--reconstruction--verified-output). Input: the coordinator's `next` is the largest repeated empty-queue overlap on `mozilla` (doc/profiling/decode-waits.md#ranked-disposition), yet moving body reads to workers removed 96% of admission CPU without a wall gain (doc/profiling/decode-positioned0.sol.md#clean-gate-no-qualifying-speedup). Output: an untimed strace counted 814 Rust writes against 203 for C on the 12-frame bundle (design/decode-throughput/design0.astra.md#two-short-checks-with-the-saved-binaries); sink controls have not resolved a wall effect (doc/profiling/decode-waits.md#follow-up-vary-input-and-output-separately), and regular-file output was measured only for the pool study (doc/profiling/decode-pool.md#confirmation-full-concat-sweep-and-regular-file-output). Split kernel/user transfers from user-space passes before proposing a change.

title: Reduce staging between entropy decode and LZ reconstruction
description: Trace RLE/Huffman literals and tokens from section expansion through block.rs reconstruction. Compare reusable section destinations or direct placement where ordering permits. PivCo internal merge copy-back belongs to zxcrs-simd-scratch.
acceptance_criteria: Measure section bytes materialized versus bytes written to final output, peak scratch and decode speed on RLE, inline and shared Huffman fixtures. Preserve checksums, malformed-section rejection and LZ overlap behavior.
notes: 2026-11-24 (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37) scope. Reusable section destinations landed: zxcrs-copies-literals-buffers (530db0a0). Lending the traversal FIFO across sections was rejected: zxcrs-copies-literals-queue (d0107ed9). What remains is the per-section order Vec, which reserves 511 slots but writes 8 on the primary workload, and compact order records; the single-variable designs are in design/pivco-metadata/assessment0.astra.md#other-bounded-designs-and-what-they-would-test. Decide zxcrs-perf-decode-compact first: it replaces the heap nodes, FIFO and reverse-order Vec with one stack array.

title: Avoid building and copying a second complete dense payload
description: Measure raw section assembly, entropy candidate materialization and dense.extend_from_slice in encode.rs and entropy/pack.rs. Try pricing sections first and serializing the winner once, or reusing final storage.
acceptance_criteria: Report bytes staged for winning and rejected candidates, peak scratch and encode rate on RAW fallback and entropy-friendly data. Preserve mode decisions, padding and archive identity.
notes: 2026-11-24 evidence (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37). At 4 KiB the initial literals and RLE candidate each copy 0.562 B/B, second dense assembly 0.441 and the Huffman candidate 0.437; at 512 KiB assembly is 0.504, just below the whole archive. "Dense assembly is worth investigating but not the highest amplification" (doc/profiling/ledger.md#interpreting-the-rankings). The proposal to price first and write winners once is rank 4 in doc/profiling/pipeline-comparison.sol.md#experiments-in-priority-order. The compact writer (e2db4d67) already shares one allocation between an inline table and its payload, but a block still reassembles into a second Vec when any section changes (doc/profiling/dense-parser.md#cost-of-emitting-the-same-huffman-sections).

description: Start with the measured PivCo hotspot. On the 1,000-frame wide-Huffman input upstream C took 28.6 ms with explicit kernels and 82.8 ms without; this is motivation, not a predicted Rust speedup. Evidence: doc/profiling/README.md.
acceptance_criteria: Record keep/drop decisions per candidate. Compare whole-archive throughput on the wide fixture and a second representative input; retain scalar fallback, valid/invalid conformance and generated C interop for adopted kernels.
notes:
2026-11-23 SIMD outcome of the decode throughput pass (opencode://ses_df8fd29afffepXs04yCk9DZsqv). Account: design/decode-throughput/handoff0.sol.md.

Flat unpack, zxcrs-simd-flat: the width-three x86 shuffle 845a76c6 (earlier) and the width-six AVX2 kernel 0d68cb82 landed. Width six on ARM64 NEON landed in 2474ff3d through Fearless SIMD concat swizzle, two TBL4 per 32 symbols. Width five is the next measured candidate, 4.97M single literal symbols. Wasm simd128 and relaxed paths are unchanged.

Bitmap merge: the bounded 32-output AVX2 kernel 45415859 landed, two shuffles, a blend and one full store, with the exact eight-output suffix. Rejected with evidence: the two-group AVX2 shuffle (doc/profiling/pivco-avx2-merge0.sol.md), BMI2 PDEP (doc/profiling/bitmap-merge-race0.sol.md) and alternating scratch (doc/profiling/pivco-scratch.md).

Dispatch, zxcrs-simd-dispatch: Linux ARM64 and riscv64gc correctness now run under QEMU with and without merge-simd (96de6837, doc/testing/linux-qemu.md). There is no ARM or RISC-V performance data. Pinned fearless_simd 1.2.0 has no RVV backend, so RISC-V stays scalar.

Tracking gap: zxcrs-simd-flat and zxcrs-simd-dispatch are broader than what landed, and the rejected kernels have no tickets. The pass would map onto separate tickets for width five, an ARM NEON TBL2 merge, ARM and RISC-V timing, and each rejected kernel.
2026-11-24 (opencode://ses_df3d97c48ffefOBHZ82w2odR37): tracking gap closed. zxcrs-simd-flat now holds zxcrs-simd-flat3 and zxcrs-simd-flat-neon (landed) and zxcrs-simd-flat5 (open). zxcrs-simd-dispatch holds zxcrs-simd-dispatch-qemu (landed) and keeps real-hardware timing. zxcrs-simd-merge-pair records the rejected two-group shuffle and zxcrs-simd-tbl2 is the ARM64 merge candidate. Width-six AVX2 and the bounded AVX2 merge are under zxcrs-perf-decode.

title: Capture checked decode phases in C and Rust with a paired Tracy fork
description:
The Rust-only Tracy smoke could not say whether materializing sections or reconstructing output takes longer in C on the same checked blocks. Build a small local C fork at the performance pin behind a private `ZXC_PROFILE_TRACY` option, and a `decode-tracy/v1` boundary map that binds six semantic IDs to source sites in each implementation: block.checked, spl.payload, spl.reconstruct, the two inline Huffman sections and block.hash. Share a definition of work, not a tracing library between languages, and capture each implementation separately.

The paired runner verifies what was traced: tool versions and protocol headers before any workload, exact plaintext through EOF, expected zone counts and nesting, a corrupted-checksum negative with the same output prefix, and timeout behavior without a collector. Section preparation is derived from each reconstruct-start minus payload-start pair, not from a new probe.

Result: an exact attached pair on `sao` W1 and `single` W8, with off and detached controls. C built with the option off is byte-identical to the stock C CLI. The captures are uncalibrated and qualitative only, because the overhead gate has not run.

One exact attached C and Rust pair on sao W1 and one on single W8, with negatives. Ship the overhead protocol and label traces uncalibrated unless its gate ran.

title: Handle short one-byte match extensions directly in the SPL16 fallback
description:
An exact count on the pinned C7 files found 254,528 extended matches of length 20-64 on `mozilla` and 345,106 on `webster`; almost every extension fits in one byte, and `sao` C7 has none. After the inline batch misses, handle the 20-64 byte case with a short literal count, a checked logical budget, a nonoverlapping logical match and space in initialized scratch for the fixed-width copies. Only a successful copy consumes an extension byte. Broadening both lanes of the ordinary pair slowed the predominantly inline C3 `webster` path, so extension handling stays outside that pair.

Result: a modest targeted improvement, not a clean aggregate win. A 25-pass C7 sweep took 161.93 to 158.08 ms per pass; a 21-pass check gave C7 176.75 to 174.44 ms, C3 104.11 to 101.77 ms and Rust Dense 193.20 to 190.02 ms, while 21 mixed fallback controls went from 265.82 to 271.33 ms. A later seven-pass comparison on two files did not reproduce an aggregate speedup.

title: Try an ARM64 NEON two-register table merge
description:
On AArch64 NEON, TBL2 indexes two 16-byte registers directly for 16 outputs, using the same selector rows as the x86 lanes: one table lookup replaces two shuffles and a blend. It is a plausible native candidate, not a measured requirement.

Measure the existing ARM64 kernel on real hardware first (zxcrs-simd-dispatch). Compare with today's NEON merge on that hardware, with the same 16-byte physical guard or an interior-and-suffix proof. Keep the explicit SIMD128 and relaxed SIMD Wasm components on their tested indices 0-15, and the unflagged component on its scalar cursor.

description:
The Codec checks workflow cross-builds the codec tests and runs the Linux ELF binaries under QEMU user-mode. Each run verifies the vendored fixture hashes and runs codec unit and integration tests in locked release builds, first with merge-simd, then without.

Covers Linux/glibc codec correctness. It is not CLI behavior on other systems and not performance on real hardware.

title: Decode six-bit flat groups with ARM64 NEON
description:
Share the bounded 24-byte index extraction with the AVX2 kernel and use Fearless SIMD concat swizzle for the NEON 64-entry lookup: exactly 24 readable bytes for 32 symbols, two four-register tbl instructions per group and an exact tail. QEMU exercised the real NEON dispatch; x86 AVX2 release kernel instructions and constants compare unchanged. RISC-V keeps the portable path, because pinned Fearless SIMD 1.2.0 has no RVV backend.

Landed for correctness only. There is no native ARM64 performance evidence, and emulation cannot establish throughput.

description:
